researched.name: SPML Infra Ltd
researched.reason: Score 7 on the scan, and the only candidate of the 46 whose own documents supported a card. Q2 FY27 standalone revenue from operations Rs 234.35 cr (+23.3% YoY) with PAT Rs 22.23 cr (+45.8%) - and the single most useful thing found this run is that **the gap between those two is a nil tax charge**: PBT grew 15.6%, and SPML bore no tax at all in FY26, Q1 FY27 or Q2 FY27 while Q2 FY26 bore Rs 3.97 cr. Published anyway because the rest is real and documented: H1 operating cash flow +Rs 82.4 cr against -Rs 44.1 cr, cash Rs 119.24 cr (+88% on 31-Mar-2026), total borrowings Rs 313.63 cr against Rs 345.62 cr so net debt about Rs 108 cr on net worth of Rs 1,184.59 cr, EBITDA margin 11.0% vs 10.0%, ICRA upgraded to BBB (Stable) and CRISIL assigning the same, a 2.5 GWh BESS line at Supa MIDC 'fully ready' with CWIP up from Rs 64.21 cr to Rs 156.81 cr in the half and an NTPC Rs 1,128 cr anchor order whose advance is received - all while the share is **down 26.8% over a year**. The card is published with the four things that argue the other way stated in full: the tax artefact above; **the order book has stopped growing** (Rs 5,100 cr on 17-Aug to Rs 5,056 cr on 30-Sep while Rs 234 cr was executed, implying roughly Rs 190 cr of Q2 intake by our own arithmetic against an FY27 call of 'more than INR5,000 crores'); the FY26 annual report's note 17.3, under which a default on the Rs 700 cr NARCL settlement reinstates **Rs 2,604.52 cr** - about 2.2x net worth and 1.9x market cap; and a Q2 FY27 limited review that did not review **12 joint operations carrying Rs 230.29 cr of H1 revenue, 44.4% of the standalone half**, with 2 more unreviewed and 5 left out of the statement altogether. Also stated: 267 days of receivables; a 13.50% promoter pledge under the Master Restructuring Agreement with NARCL holding shares to keep its own 12.50%; a first-ranking charge over all receivables INCLUDING the arbitration awards and over all BESS project assets; the claims figure moving from Rs 4,526 cr (Aug call) to Rs 3,857 cr (deck) to 'approximately Rs 3,827 crore' (press release) with the last two filed the SAME day; the deck's 'New Order Wins (Total) Rs 5,802.81 cr' being gross of JV partners, about Rs 4,466 cr at SPML's own stated shares; and **6 distinct order announcements in the 730 days to 13-Nov-2026** (read from all 239 of its BSE announcements), which puts it nearer the order study's serial-bidder end than its rare-filer end, with the latest order worth 17.9% of a trailing year's sales - below the 25-50% band. On a tax-normalised trailing PAT of about Rs 65 cr the PE is ~21x against peers at 8.6-15.4x, so the card says explicitly that the case cannot be 'a cheap EPC'.

researched.name: Vikran Engineering Ltd
researched.verdict: NOT PUBLISHED - a guidance gap the company could not close on its own call
researched.reason: The Q2/H1 FY27 earnings-call transcript was filed at 19:41 today and reads well on the order book - **Rs 6,200 cr**, roughly 30% of it T&D substation EPC with price-escalation clauses on everything except solar - but badly on everything else. Consolidated Q2 revenue Rs 211.84 cr against Rs 176 cr (+20%), while **EBITDA FELL to Rs 22.26 cr from Rs 25.43 cr and the margin to 10.5% from 14.4%**, with management guiding 'around 15% odd' going forward. The decisive exchange is an investor's own arithmetic, which management did not dispute: H1 revenue is **Rs 424 cr against an annual guidance of about Rs 2,300 cr, so H2 alone would have to deliver Rs 1,875 cr** - 4.4x the half just reported. The answer given was that Q2 had been targeted at ~Rs 500 cr and 'we have slipped'. A company 18% of the way to its own full-year number with one half left is a guidance-credibility problem, not an idea. X leads, unverified against filings this run and recorded as such: a Rs 3,517.98 cr Maharashtra solar EPC win, and a ~Rs 1,641.91 cr LOA accepted on 10 November and then 'mutually cancelled' after an internal evaluation - if that second one is real it belongs on any future card, and it is the first thing to check from the filings next time this name comes up.
